detail: Bare `reproit init` classified a backend-only repository as a web UI project whenever its one browser-shaped marker was the page the service itself serves. A raw node:http server with a minimal package.json and an index.html in the root got app.platform: web, a Playwright runner, journeys and devices blocks, and url: http://localhost:3000 as a guess: confident, plausible, and the wrong workflow entirely. Two causes, both closed here. node:http was not in the recognised framework list, because it is stdlib and therefore invisible in package.json, which is exactly why the old error text advertised Go's net/http while node's http module went unread. And project_scaffold::detect consulted web markers before backend detection, so index.html decided the platform before anything asked whether the repo was a service. The defect is in pure detection with no process, network, or filesystem dependency beyond a temporary fixture directory, so a bounded unit test over the exact repository shape is the stable reproduction authority: it fails on the parent with `left: Some(Web), right: None` and passes on the fix. The gate compiles this test from scratch in a worktree, so the dogfood-policy job needs the Rust toolchain and the CLI's Linux system libraries; without them the build fails and the gate misreports it as a fixed-side test failure. Re-measured against rebuilt fixtures in validation/field/init-ground-truth.md.
